family.description: This family includes prokaryotic proteins of unknown function, as well as a protein annotated as the pit accessory protein from Sinorhizobium meliloti [swissprot:O30498]. However, the function of this protein is also unknown (Pit stands for Phosphate transport). It is probably distantly related to [pfam:PF01895] (personal obs:Yeats C).
family.name: Protein of unknown function DUF47

Added eight phenotypic graphs with seventeen indirect observed effects, retaining operon polarity, protein-state alternatives, nonzero mutant residuals, combined genotype scope and exopolyphosphatase readout limits. Baseline 8296 records valid with zero drift. Remaining member and context evidence is follow-up; retain IN_PROGRESS. No publication authorized.

causal_graphs.context: S. meliloti RmP3924 delta-pap in the conditional Pho-regulon background; no IPTG after depletion. Growth in MOPS-P2, 20 mM glucose and 2 mM Pi at 30 C; separate 33P uptake assay at 10 uM Pi. Compare operon-restoring integration with pap-only integration.

evidence.explanation: Original Figures3-15A/3-16A-C, printed103-104, show the growth comparisons and PCR-distinguished recombinant architectures; Methods and strain table constrain scope.

edges.mechanism: The operon-restoring recombinant recovers the growth trajectory of the full pap-pit control. The alternative split-promoter recombinant does not rescue, so this is not proof of a direct Pap-to-Pit activation step.
edges.subject: restore-operon

evidence.explanation: Original Figure3-15B, printed103; uptake Methods2.10 distinguishes the 10 uM assay from growth at 2 mM Pi.

edges.mechanism: Operon-restored uptake is 3.48 versus pap-only 0.78 nmol Pi/mg protein/min; full pap-pit gives 3.13. Figure3-15B assigns restored and pap-only values to different ANOVA/Tukey groups. Transport is measured in cells, not reconstituted Pap.
edges.subject: restore-operon

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Pap O30498 sequence version 1 equals NP_384293.1, smc02862, 214 aa, PF01865 4-212. Rm1021-derived experimental strains, not an isolated domain.
causal_graphs.limitations: Restoration includes operon architecture and downstream pit expression. Pap alone is not sufficient. Polar effects remain unresolved; native transporter abundance is not established. Methods/Table2-1 disagree on phnC versus phoC background naming.

causal_graphs.context: RmP3926 delta-pap-pit, conditional Pho-regulon background, pUCP30T-derived native-promoter operons. Growth at 30 C in MOPS-P2 with 2 mM Pi; separate uptake at 10 uM Pi. Each variant compared with WT pap-pit.

evidence.explanation: Original Figure3-21A, printed109, visually inspected; Table2-4 defines the individual mutant constructs.

edges.mechanism: Each single variant grows more slowly than the matched WT operon in the displayed time course. P75A eventually approaches the WT OD, preventing an interpretation of complete growth loss.
edges.subject: pap-single-substitution

evidence.explanation: Original Table3-21B, printed109, with Results3.2.2 contradiction explicitly retained.

edges.mechanism: P75A gives 0.198 +/-0.124 and R78A 0.983 +/-0.502 versus WT 3.12 +/-0.142 nmol Pi/mg protein/min, reported SD. The table's nonzero R78A value takes precedence over the prose's no-uptake wording.
edges.subject: pap-single-substitution

causal_graphs.family_mapping: O30498/NP_384293.1 Pap; PF01865 4-212 includes reference P75 and R78. Grouped node denotes separate single mutants, not a double mutant.
causal_graphs.limitations: Whole-cell effects may involve protein abundance, folding or downstream Pit translation. Positive residual uptake is not zero transport. Growth delay is not a permanent inability to grow, and statistical significance is not asserted for unmarked comparisons.

causal_graphs.title: P75A and R78A alter native-host growth and phosphate uptake

causal_graphs.context: E. coli MT2006, MG1655-derived delta-pitA/delta-pitB/delta-phnC/delta-(pstSCAB-phoU); pUC119 lac-driven SmPapPit versus empty pUC119. 10 uM 33P-Pi assay at 37 C; biological triplicates, protein-normalized initial slope.

evidence.explanation: Original Table3-28, printed116; Tables2-1/2-4 and Methods2.10 establish host, vector, substrate and readout.

edges.mechanism: Uptake is 27.4 +/-3.16 with pTH2826 versus empty pUC119 0.348 +/-0.119 nmol Pi/mg protein/min, reported SD. Both Pap and Pit and the expression context are part of the intervention.
edges.subject: high-copy-pap-pit

causal_graphs.family_mapping: S. meliloti Pap O30498/NP_384293.1, PF01865 4-212, expressed with its Pit partner in E. coli. Taxon identifies the donor reference, not the heterologous host.
causal_graphs.limitations: Not Pap-only sufficiency. Low-copy pMW119 SmPapPit did not show the same rescue. This uptake comparison is not growth in M9 with approximately 69 mM Pi or evidence that Pap itself transports phosphate.

causal_graphs.context: MT2006 with pUC119 lac-driven intact SmPapPit, each mutant compared with WT pTH2826. 10 uM 33P-Pi, 37 C; protein-normalized initial uptake, biological triplicates.

evidence.explanation: Original Table3-28 and Figure3-29, printed116-117; assay reduction is not an independently demonstrated catalytic or metal-binding mechanism.

edges.mechanism: Point estimates are E54A 4.61, D58A 2.00, P75A 2.38, R78A 0.629 and D93A 1.23 versus WT 27.4 nmol Pi/mg protein/min. Each is a separate comparison; retained source lists SDs and no exact mechanistic ranking is inferred.
edges.subject: single-variants

evidence.explanation: Table3-28 quantitative rows and Table2-4 combined construct identity; Results printed50 uses incompatible zero-uptake language.

edges.mechanism: D90A/H96Y gives 7.86 +/-0.590 versus WT 27.4 +/-3.16, reported SD. Single D90A gives 25.1 +/-2.55. The combined result cannot establish H96Y alone, and contradicts the prose's no-uptake wording.
edges.subject: double-variant

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Pap O30498/NP_384293.1 reference numbering; PF01865 4-212 includes E54,D58,P75,R78,D93,D90,H96. D90A/H96Y is a double mutant, not an H96Y single-mutant test.
causal_graphs.limitations: Grouped node denotes five separate single mutants. Figure3-29 shows altered Pap bands for some variants; abundance, processing, folding and Pit translation remain alternatives to a catalytic-site effect. The reported double-mutant residual is not zero.

evidence.explanation: Original Figure2A, 5 mM Pi single-mutant versus WT bars, and growth/expression Methods.

edges.mechanism: The single deletion increases normalized pst reporter output relative to WT in this high-Pi condition; the molecular route remains unresolved.
edges.subject: delete-pitr

evidence.explanation: Original Figure2B, 5 mM Pi comparison; at least three biological replicates and the reported statistical analysis.

edges.mechanism: The single deletion increases normalized nptA reporter output relative to WT; this is not a measured phosphate transport rate.
edges.subject: delete-pitr

evidence.explanation: Original Figure2E single delta-pitR paired bars, not the higher-order mutant comparisons.

edges.mechanism: PitR complementation reduces the elevated pst reporter relative to the empty-vector deletion strain. It supports genotype attribution without identifying a direct signaling interaction.
edges.subject: restore-pitr

evidence.explanation: Original Figure2D paired single-mutant complementation comparison.

edges.mechanism: Complementation reduces the elevated nptA reporter toward the WT vector-control level under the matched high-Pi condition.

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Newman NWMN_0632/BAF66904.1, 205 aa, exactly matches UniParc UPI00000549A3 with PF01865 2-202. This is the reference sequence, not an independently resequenced laboratory stock.
causal_graphs.limitations: Reporter output is not direct PhoPR phosphorylation, promoter binding or physical PitA inhibition. Whole-gene perturbation does not establish isolated-domain sufficiency. Effects are conditional on medium and Pi concentration.

edges.mechanism: The single mutant has increased nptA reporter output relative to WT at intermediate Pi; no transport-rate or free-phosphate measurement is implied.

edges.mechanism: The PitR plasmid lowers nptA reporter output relative to the mutant's empty-vector control, consistent with complementation in this genetic background.

causal_graphs.context: Newman delta-pitR phoU::erm, labeled delta-pitR delta-phoU in the paper; PFM9 pH7.4, 5 mM Pi, 37 C. OD600 growth time course and a separate protein-normalized lysate assay after exopolyphosphatase treatment.

evidence.explanation: Original Figure3A double-mutant trajectory and single-mutant controls; Methods specifies the phoU::erm allele.

edges.mechanism: The combined mutant enters growth later than WT at 5 mM Pi but approaches a similar final OD. The phenotype cannot be assigned to loss of PitR alone or to a specific biochemical intermediate.
edges.subject: combined-loss

evidence.explanation: Original Figure3G and phosphate-assay Methods; at least five biological replicates and the reported ANOVA/Tukey comparison.

edges.mechanism: The double mutant gives more phosphate per total protein than WT in the 5 mM condition. Exopolyphosphatase pretreatment means the assay does not separate free Pi from polyphosphate-derived Pi; the 500 uM comparison is not increased.
edges.subject: combined-loss

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Only PitR BAF66904.1/UPI00000549A3 is mapped here to PF01865 2-202. Conventional PhoU is a second regulator, not another mapped PF01865 member.
causal_graphs.limitations: Joint loss is the intervention; single delta-pitR does not establish either effect. The lysate readout includes polyphosphate-derived Pi, not free cytosolic Pi or uptake velocity. These assays do not establish that an enlarged phosphate pool causes the growth delay.

edges.mechanism: The corresponding 500 uM Pi experiment also shows restoration of the double-mutant growth trajectory. This does not imply a phosphate-pool change, which is not elevated in that concentration's separate assay.

causal_graphs.family_mapping: PitR NWMN_0632/BAF66904.1, exact UPI00000549A3 sequence, PF01865 2-202; the phoU::erm background remains part of both comparisons.
causal_graphs.limitations: Growth rescue is not a directly measured rescue of the phosphate-pool assay or a physical PitR-PhoU interaction. Final biomass and lag are different outcomes. The source's 500 mM prose typo is not adopted; figure axes specify 500 uM.

record.description: This family includes prokaryotic proteins of unknown function, as well as a protein annotated as the pit accessory protein from Sinorhizobium meliloti [swissprot:O30498]. However, the function of this protein is also unknown (Pit stands for Phosphate transport). It is probably distantly related to [pfam:PF01895] (personal obs:Yeats C).

evidence.explanation: Figures3-15/16/21/29 and Table3-28 establish the retained effects and expose prose/table and protein-band discrepancies.

discussions.notes: See evidence/PF01865/phou-div-gap-ledger.txt. Resolve P75mis/P75fs identity, phnC/phoC naming, remaining variants and heterologous member mappings. Do not convert dimerization or an unidentified-ligand model into observed activation.
discussions.prompt: Resolve operon polarity and protein-state effects before assigning a direct Pap mechanism.
discussions.rationale: Operon rescue and substitutions support scoped whole-cell effects, while pap-only failure and altered bands prevent a direct isolated-domain activation claim.

evidence.explanation: Retained edges distinguish single and combined genotypes, Pi concentrations, reporter output, growth timing and exopolyphosphatase-treated lysate phosphate.

discussions.notes: Supplement FigureS1 and TablesS2-S4 confirm the PitR locus, strain backgrounds and plasmid design; independent clone-sequence checks, environmental and higher-order contexts, and member-specific follow-up remain. USA500 PhoU2, dimerization and evolved-isolate studies are leads, not completed graph assessments. Keep IN_PROGRESS.

discussions.rationale: Newman reporter and combined-genotype effects do not exhaust family evidence or establish direct phosphate sensing.
